jobs.title: PACE Home Care Coordinator
jobs.description:
Position Summary

As a collaborative member of the interdisciplinary team (IDT), and under the supervision of the Home Care Coordination RN Manager, this role provides foundational support to the Home Care Coordination team. The position involves conducting home safety evaluations, coordinating and monitoring IDT-approved services such as meal delivery, caregiver services, and durable medical equipment (DME) for program participants. The role advocates for participants' healthcare needs and preferences, ensuring that care is delivered in a person-centered and compassionate manner. It requires working closely with participants, their families, and the interdisciplinary team to ensure all aspects of unskilled home-based care are coordinated and aligned with the participants' goals and preferences.

Essential Functions Of The Job

Coordinate IDT-approved meal delivery to client homes.
Coordinate IDT-approved Durable Medical Equipment and incontinence supply delivery to client homes.
Coordinate IDT-approved caregiver services for participants.
Complete the Home Care Coordination care plan at enrollment and semi-annually thereafter.
Conduct pre-enrollment, annual, semi-annual, and change of address home safety evaluations.
Document and track actions, services, and service delivery status updates in designated logs and participant electronic medical records (EMR) in accordance with clinical, DHCS, and CMS regulations and guidelines.
Review progress notes and documentation of the delivery of services, informing the IDT of any gaps in service for reconciliation.
Upload progress notes, reports, and care/vendor-related documentation to the EMR.
Communicate regularly with participants, their families, and other healthcare providers to ensure coordinated care delivery.
Advocate for participants' healthcare needs and preferences, ensuring that care is delivered in a person-centered and compassionate manner.
Provide support to nurses in the coordination and delivery of meals, DME, caregiver services, etc.
Collaborate with interdisciplinary team members, including physicians, social workers, therapists, and other healthcare professionals, to ensure coordinated care for participants.
Adhere to infectious disease precautions to prevent the spread of organisms.
Attend center staff meetings and in-service educational training programs.
Assist Home Care Coordination RNs as requested.
Conduct and document monthly visits for homebound and RCFE participants.
Conduct home visits as needed.
Assist participants with surveys.
Deliver supplies, equipment, grocery bags, and any other items as requested/needed.
Generate and maintain reports of services provided for the participants.

Additional Duties And Responsibilities

Communicate and work effectively with participants and co-workers.
Participate in interdisciplinary team meetings as needed.
Adhere to attendance and punctuality policies and practices.
Follow established departmental and position-specific policies and procedures.
Attend meetings as required and participate in committees as directed.
Maintain health and safety standards and take an active role in the Safety and Injury Prevention in the Workplace Program; maintain all records and documentation as required.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.

Minimum Qualifications

Must possess a Home Health Aide certificate and CNA certificate.
Must possess the skills necessary to coordinate and evaluate services for geriatric participants.
Must have a firm understanding of the Home Health Aide scope of practice and operate only within scope.
Must be able to communicate clearly and function well in a team environment.

Job Requirements

Education Required: Must have CNA and California Department of Public Health Home Health Aide certificate (HHA). Must have CPR and First Aid certification from the American Heart Association.
Experience Required: One year experience with the frail or elderly population. Valid California Driver's License.
Technical Knowledge and Skills: Basic computer skills, Microsoft, Outlook, Excel.

Working Conditions and Physical Requirements

Pre-employment requirements include I-9, physical, positive background and reference check results, complete application, new hire orientation, pre-employment PPDs.
Compliance with all mandated vaccinations and all boosters is a term and condition of employment.

Compliance

Maintain privacy of all patients, employee, and volunteer information and access such information only on a need-to-know basis for business purposes.
Comply with all regulations regarding corporate integrity and security obligations. Report unethical, fraudulent, or unlawful behavior or activity.
Comply with all regulations and required schedules regarding OSHA training.
Required health screening to be performed annually.
Responsible for following all policies and procedures.
Comply with all regulations and required schedules regarding sexual harassment training.

jobs.title: Senior Strategist; Program Manager
jobs.description:
Who We Are:
LINK is a fast-growing Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB) that leverages human-centered design to support strategy, innovation, communication, change, and branding within the federal government and adjacent industry partners. At LINK, we partner with engineers, futurists, and thought leaders to untangle complexity, discover opportunity, and communicate clearly with visual stories.

Let us be your partners in change.

Location:
We are actively hiring in the San Diego area.

About The Opportunity

LINK is actively seeking a Senior Strategist; Program Manager
to join our dynamic team, where we leverage strong partnerships and a robust portfolio of clients across diverse industries. You will be responsible for leading and executing innovative design strategies, collaborating with both internal teams and executive-level clients, and driving impactful visual storytelling to meet client objectives.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced professional to bring a combination of creative and strategic expertise to elevate LINK’s business growth and deliver high-quality, human-centered design solutions. You will work closely with clients to understand their challenges, develop compelling narratives, and implement design strategies that align with their mission, goals, and brand identity. Ideal candidates will have a proven track record of designing impactful visual experiences, utilizing data-driven insights, and collaborating cross-functionally to deliver exceptional client results.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Journalism, Communication, English, Business, or a related field
10+ years of experience in strategic communication, public affairs, program management, or strategy development
7+ years program/project management experience including familiarity with Agile methodologies and project delivery best practices
Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, maintaining a strong focus on accuracy and attention to detail
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate in a clear, approachable, and knowledgeable manner
Government contracting experience
PMP certification preferred
Experience with human-centered design and design thinking principles
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex projects simultaneously

Responsibilities

Senior Strategist responsibilities include:

Client Partnership & Design Strategy Leadership

Serves as a trusted advisor to clients by framing complex challenges, identifying opportunities, and applying human-centered design approaches to inform strategic decision-making.
Partners directly with client stakeholders to understand organizational priorities, user needs, operational constraints, and desired outcomes.
Leads the development of design strategy approaches that align stakeholder needs, business objectives, and mission requirements.
Guides cross-functional teams through ambiguity, helping stakeholders build alignment and make informed decisions.
Identifies opportunities to create tangible business value and support long-term client success.
Provides guidance that helps clients make informed decisions and navigate organizational complexity.

Content Strategy, Storytelling & Execution

Translates complex ideas into compelling strategic narratives, executive-level presentations, communication strategies, and decision-support products.
Develops messaging frameworks that align leadership vision, organizational priorities, and stakeholder needs.
Define content structures, information hierarchies, and storytelling approaches that communicate complex concepts clearly and effectively.
Collaborates with creative teams to develop high-quality visual products that support strategic objectives and audience understanding.
Establishes quality standards for strategic deliverables and provides guidance to team members to ensure consistency and excellence.
Leads development of executive-ready materials that support decision-making, alignment, and organizational action.

Change Management & Organizational Transformation

Develops and implements change management strategies, including stakeholder engagement plans, communications strategies, change impact assessments, and adoption roadmaps.
Designs governance frameworks, operating models, and implementation approaches that support successful transformation efforts.
Facilitates cross-functional working sessions that drive alignment, accelerate decision-making, and address organizational resistance.
Establishes feedback mechanisms and performance measures that support continuous improvement and long-term success.
Monitors progress, evaluates outcomes, and refines approaches based on stakeholder feedback and organizational needs.

Research, Insight Development & Systems Thinking

Leads mixed-method research efforts, including stakeholder interviews, contextual inquiry, observations, journey mapping, ecosystem analysis, and systems mapping activities.
Synthesizes qualitative and quantitative findings into actionable insights, opportunity areas, strategic recommendations, and design directions.
Applies systems thinking to identify patterns, dependencies, root causes, and opportunities across complex organizational environments.
Translates technical, operational, and policy-focused challenges into human-centered insights and strategic considerations.
Guides research activities that inform organizational transformation, service design, experience design, and strategic planning efforts.

Workshop Facilitation & Stakeholder Alignment

Designs and facilitates workshops, design sprints, stakeholder engagements, and co-creation activities that advance strategic objectives and drive organizational alignment.
Develops facilitation approaches, agendas, exercises, and collaborative experiences that enable productive dialogue and structured problem-solving.
Synthesizes workshop outputs into actionable findings, recommendations, and implementation considerations.
Helps stakeholders navigate competing priorities, organizational complexity, and change initiatives through structured facilitation and engagement.
Guides teams in applying human-centered design methods throughout project lifecycles.

Team Development & Leadership

Mentors teammates through coaching, knowledge sharing, and constructive feedback.
Models LINK values and contributes to a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing team culture.
Shares tools, approaches, and lessons learned that improve the quality and consistency of work across engagements.

Program Manager Responsibilities Include

Client & Program Leadership

Serve as the primary point of accountability for contract performance, client satisfaction, financial health, and delivery success.
Maintain strong client relationships and serve as a trusted advisor to client stakeholders.
Collaborate with clients to understand challenges, define priorities, manage expectations, and identify opportunities to create additional value.
Lead strategic planning activities and establish program priorities, objectives, and delivery approaches.
Identify opportunities to extend existing work and support business development efforts within client organizations.

Team Leadership & Coordination

Establish delivery priorities and provide direction to project teams in support of contract objectives.
Oversee onboarding, offboarding, and transition activities for project team members.
Provide coaching and feedback focused on delivery excellence, client satisfaction, and team effectiveness.
Coordinate with Competency Managers and contribute project performance observations and feedback to support employee development and performance management processes.

Delivery & Operational Excellence

Oversee program budgets, team utilization, schedules, staffing plans, risks, subcontractor performance, and deliverable quality.
Establish and maintain project management processes, Agile cadences, reporting mechanisms, and communication rhythms to ensure effective delegation of tasks, workload management, and on-time delivery.
Ensure successful execution of contractual requirements, deliverables, reporting obligations, and period of performance requirements.
Monitor program health and proactively identify risks, issues, and opportunities requiring leadership attention.
Coordinate invoicing, reporting, travel, security, and operational activities necessary to support successful contract execution.
Document and share lessons learned, best practices, and operational improvements that strengthen delivery effectiveness.

Work Schedule

Full time, 40 hours per week
Some travel required to attend relevant events and conferences, and participate in LINK team events

Salary:
We're committed to offering competitive compensation. While the salary range for this position is $112,000-$151,000

Benefits

$100 monthly internet/cell phone stipend
$150 monthly commuter stipend for eligible participants
LINK sponsored healthcare benefits including medical, dental, vision

jobs.title: Employee Engagement Program Manager
jobs.description:
Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.

If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.

Note: This position requires presence in our San Francisco/San Jose/Bellevue office location 4 days per week; Lambda’s designated work from home day is currently Tuesday.

We’ve built a lot of great resources for employees: onboarding guides, benefits pages, manager how-tos, and hiring FAQs. But we move faster than we document and maintain. We’re growing quickly. Things get out of date, hard to find, or inconsistent in tone. We need someone to own that problem end to end and make sure every piece of employee-facing content is accurate, easy to find, and sounds like it came from the same team.

This isn’t a pure technical writing role, and it isn’t a traditional program management role either. It’s both. You’ll write, design, and edit, but you’ll also audit, organize, and measure. If you like bringing order to scattered information and quietly making everyone’s job a little easier (maybe even delightful), this is your gig.

What You’ll Do

Audit employee-facing pages, websites, FAQs, guides, and policies.
Write and edit onboarding guides, templates, FAQs, and how-tos.
Set consistent tone, voice, and format across content.
Organize content so employees can find answers.
Fix pages and processes when something isn't working.
Track usage and feedback to see what’s working and what isn’t.
Coordinate with HR, Talent, on shared content.

What You’ll Bring

3 to 5 years in writing, content, or program coordination.
Strong, clear, creative writing and editing skills.
Comfort building style guides and content standards.
A sharp eye for content that’s outdated or hard to find.
Comfort tracking metrics like page views, clicks, comments, reactions.
Nice to have: experience with Notion, Confluence, Wikis.

Why You’ll Love It Here

You’ll have a front-row seat to the growth of a company shaping the future of tech, and you’ll have a direct hand in making that growth possible. We value speed, tenacity, creativity, and being excellent to each other. You’ll be a part of the Employee Engagement team. Our goal is simple: to be the most helpful team at Lambda. If you want a seat where you can make a huge impact every day and turn chaos into clarity, this is it.

Salary Range Information

The annual salary range for this position has been set based on market data and other factors. However, a salary higher or lower than this range may be appropriate for a candidate whose qualifications differ meaningfully from those listed in the job description.

About Lambda

Founded in 2012, with 500+ employees, and growing fast
Our investors notably include TWG Global, US Innovative Technology Fund (USIT), Andra Capital, SGW, Andrej Karpathy, ARK Invest, Fincadia Advisors, G Squared, In-Q-Tel (IQT), KHK & Partners, NVIDIA, Pegatron, Supermicro, Wistron, Wiwynn, Gradient Ventures, Mercato Partners, SVB, 1517, and Crescent Cove
We have research papers accepted at top machine learning and graphics conferences, including NeurIPS, ICCV, SIGGRAPH, and TOG
Our values are publicly available: https://lambda.ai/careers
We offer generous cash & equity compensation
Health, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents
Wellness and commuter stipends for select roles
401k Plan with 2% company match (USA employees)
Flexible paid time off plan that we all actually use

Equal Opportunity Employer

Applicants are considered without regard to race, color, religion, creed, national origin, age, sex, gender, marital status, sexual orientation and identity, genetic information, veteran status, citizenship, or any other factors prohibited by local, state, or federal law.

jobs.title: Supply Chain Program Manager
jobs.description:
WD is building the infrastructure behind the AI-driven data economy.

As AI scales, so does data. Every interaction, every model, every system generates data that must be stored, managed, and made accessible over time. That’s where we come in.

We combine deep engineering expertise with global-scale manufacturing to deliver the storage systems that make AI possible, powering hyperscale data centers, cloud platforms, and enterprise infrastructure worldwide.

This isn’t theoretical work. It’s real systems, at real scale, people solving some of the hardest challenges in technology today.

We’re looking for people who want to build, solve, and operate at that level.

Join us and let’s shape the future of data.

Job Description

As a Supply Chain Program Manager in the Supply Chain Center of Excellence, you will work alongside some of the most experienced and accomplished minds across Western Digital's Supply Chain functions, while engaging with the newest and most cutting-edge ideas in the field. Your role is to bring the two together, combining proven expertise with emerging thinking so that they work in harmony and deliver results.

You will be awarded opportunities across the full spectrum of Supply Chain functions, engaging with established leaders in Logistics, Direct Procurement, Indirect Procurement, Planning, Risk and Resiliency, Operations and beyond. Rather than relying on authority, you will build consensus through influence and persuasion, grounded in both hard facts and qualitative insight. Success depends on strong dependency management, stakeholder alignment and clear communication across functions that may have other priorities.

How we Operate

These are the behaviors expected every day. They map to the WD Leadership Expectations and define the standard that this position role models for the wider team.

Own the outcome, not the tracker. The plan is an instrument. The measure is whether the ramp landed on time, at cost and at quality.
Champion clear decisions. Most Program delay is undecided, not unknown. Frame the choice, name the decider, get it made and record it.
Manage the seams. Functions are usually competent inside their own boundary. Programs fail between them, which is where the Program Manager works.
Escalate early with a recommendation. Raise it when there is still room to act, and bring the option you would choose.
Be direct and transparent about status. Green that turns red without warning destroys credibility permanently. Report what is, not what is hoped.
Influence without direct line authority. Nobody on the Program reports to you. Credibility, preparation and reliability are the only levers — build them deliberately.
Close the loop. A Program that ends without lessons captured has spent the organization’s learning and kept none of it

Key Responsibilities

Strong Program Management Skills

Integrated planning and governance. Own the master plan, milestones, dependencies, owners, RAID log and steering committee cadence across all workstreams, with an independent view of status.
Scope, schedule and budget control. Protect the baseline, manage change through a disciplined process, and keep the program on time and on budget.
Risk and decision management. Surface risks early, frame decisions with options and a recommendation, and record outcomes so they are not relitigated.
Run the Program cadence at the right rhythm for the phase
Maintain a single source of truth for Program status
Define and enforce entry and exit criteria at each gate

Program Portfolio Leadership and Team Development

Own a portfolio of supply chain Programs, including major ramps and transitions of high complexity
Lead, coach and develop the Program Managers running them, building advanced proficiency across the Program management toolkit
Set the Program management standard for the function: plans, cadence, gates, reporting and post-Program review
Frame executive decisions, manage complex risk and drive cross-functional alignment without authority

Stakeholder Alignment

Cross-functional alignment. Bring together Legal, Direct Materials, Indirect Procurement, Logistics, Sales, Finance and IT, each with different contract types, risk tolerances and priorities.
Balancing competing priorities. Reconcile Legal’s risk posture, Procurement’s efficiency goals and the business’s need for speed into decisions all parties can support.
Composure with difficult stakeholders. Remain calm, respectful and fact-based when challenged; depersonalize conflict and keep the focus on outcomes.
Earned trust and sponsorship. Involve skeptics early, give them a real voice in design, and use executive sponsors and escalation paths deliberately.

Cross-Functional Dependency Management

Map dependencies across Sourcing, Engineering, Quality, Operations, Planning and suppliers
Track dependency status and drive owners to their commitments
Resolve cross-functional conflicts at the working level where possible
Escalate blocked dependencies with the decision required clearly stated

Risk and Decision Management

Maintain a live Program risk register with owners, mitigations and trigger points
Run scenario analysis on the risks that could move the Program
Frame decisions clearly: the choice, the options, the trade-offs, the recommendation, the decider
Track decisions and their rationale so they are not relitigated

Delivery and Adoption Discipline

Fit to standard. Champion out-of-the-box capability and challenge customization that adds cost and risk without clear value.
Testing and cutover. Lead system integration and user acceptance testing, data migration validation and a well-rehearsed go-live.
Adoption and value. Drive training, change champions and adoption metrics such as contract cycle time, and confirm the business case is realized.
Measure adoption and sustainment, and reinforce new behaviors until they become the way Western Digital works

Change management

Lead organizational change that turns new processes, tools and ways of working into lasting habits across the enterprise
Build a compelling case for change and inspire stakeholders at every level, from executive sponsors to frontline teams
Design adoption roadmaps with clear communication, training and engagement plans that bring people along, not just systems
Identify and empower change champions who carry new practices into their own functions and regions
Anticipate resistance early and turn skeptics into advocates through listening, evidence and quick wins

Executive Communication and Decision Framing

Report Program status honestly, concisely and consistently
Frame executive decisions with the choice, options, trade-offs and a recommendation
Run executive forums that produce decisions rather than updates
Manage expectations early rather than explaining misses afterwards
Executive communication. Deliver concise, candid status that lets sponsors act quickly and with confidence.
Governance. Run a structured governance process to include daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly core team and steering Committee meetings
Collateral development. Create update templates and work individually and with team members to create executive communication collateral

Program Analytics and Reporting

Build and maintain readiness and status dashboards
Use data rather than narrative to drive Program conversations
Track leading indicators, not just milestone completion
Adopt tooling, automation, and AI that reduce reporting effort

Post-Program Learning

Run honest post-Program reviews covering what worked and what did not
Convert lessons into process change with the relevant process owner
Share learning across the Program community
Improve templates, gates and standards based on what was learned

Business Process Transformation

Champion innovation by challenging how work is done today and envisioning how it should be done tomorrow
Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize and digitize end-to-end business processes across supply chain functions
Oversee transformation projects from concept through delivery, ensuring they meet scope, schedule and value commitments
Partner with IT and business owners to align process redesign with enabling systems, data and AI capabilities
Measure the impact of each transformation and feed the lessons into the next wave of improvement

What would success look like

Big bets that land. Bold programs and transformations delivered on time, on budget and at the quality customers expect.
Problems solved before they surface. Risks and gaps spotted early and closed well ahead of the moment they could hurt the business.
A supply chain ready for what's next. Capacity, capability and technology in place before demand arrives, not after.
Change without chaos. New processes, tools and transitions rolled out smoothly, with no disruption to customers and no value left on the table.
A voice leaders trust. Reporting so candid and reliable that there are never surprises, and status always reflects reality.
Decisions made in the room. Choices framed so clearly that leaders can act on the spot and keep momentum high.
A legacy that compounds. Every lesson turned into a lasting standard, so each program makes the next one faster, smarter and better.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, Engineering, Business or a related field
10+ years of experience in supply chain, operations or program management, including leading product ramps, technology transitions or supplier readiness in a high-tech, semiconductor or electronics manufacturing environment
A track record of leading process improvement or transformation work with measurable results
Hands-on familiarity with AI and automation, including generative AI tools, and the curiosity to apply them to real supply chain problems
Organizational change management experience
Experience leading and developing Program Managers or cross-functional teams
Demonstrated ability to frame executive decisions and influence senior stakeholders without direct authority
Strong working knowledge of supplier capacity, qualification, engineering change and end-of-life management
Proficiency with program analytics and dashboarding tools

Preferred

Master's degree or MBA
PMP, PgMP or ASCM (APICS) certification
Experience in data storage or hard disk drive supply chains
Delivering AI and machine learning use cases, such as predictive supplier risk, demand sensing and generative AI assistants
Experience with control towers, digital twins and supplier risk platforms
Setting up or maturing a Program Management Office, which ties to the next-generation PMO in the opening
Leading scenario planning, tabletop exercises or business continuity programs
A background in consulting, transformation offices or a center of excellence
Familiarity with sustainability, ESG and trade-compliance requirements
Working with global teams and Asia-based supplier networks
Change management certification (e.g., Prosci) or a record of leading large-scale adoption programs

Programs are where every part of the supply chain organization has to work as one. This role holds limited authority and all of the accountability, which makes credibility the entire currency of the role. Earn it by being prepared, being honest about status, and forcing the decisions nobody else wants to call.

In summary, the Program Manager is encouraged to bring innovation and creativity to every challenge, and fresh thinking about where the supply chain should go next will always be welcome. You will not be starting from a blank page: Western Digital is already pursuing a number of cutting-edge initiatives, and you will have the opportunity to shape, accelerate and expand them.

jobs.title: Case Manager - Developmental Disabilities
jobs.description:
Job Description

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

Conducts and documents comprehensive assessment of client and/or client’s needs.
Participates in development of client’s service plan, consistent with assessment.
Arranges for delivery of needed services, as identified in assessment.
Assists client in accessing needed services through, for example, referrals or linkages.
Monitors client’s progress by making referrals, tracking client’s appointments, performing follow-up on services rendered, and performing periodic reassessments of client’s changing needs.
Performs advocacy activities on behalf of client (e. g., writing letters to expedite entitlement payments, encouraging client or family members to advocate on own behalf).
Prepares and maintains case records documenting contacts, services needed, reports, client’s progress, etc., in accordance with SCS and regulatory standards.
Provides case consultation (i. e., consulting with service providers/collaterals in determining client’s status and progress).
Communicates with supervisor about issues related to case management, resourcing, service collaboration, and development of new resources.
Provides psychosocial education to clients and/or family members to increase their understanding of client’s illness, physical condition, or social situation.
Performs crisis assistance (i. e., intervention on behalf of client, making arrangements for emergency referrals, coordinates other needed emergency services).
May serve as Primary Case Coordinator (PCC), with volume and complexity of PCC assignments depending on incumbent’s skill and autonomy.

The intent of this job description is to provide a representative summary of the major duties and responsibilities performed by incumbents of this job. Incumbents may be requested to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically presented in this description.

EDUCATIO
N

Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Psychology, Sociology, Human Services, or related field as approved by Medicaid, or as required by applicable funding source.

Experience

Minimum of zero year’s experience in case management/service coordination with a Bachelor’s degree.
Working knowledge of mental and physical characteristics of assigned population group (e. g., growth and development), human behavior, treatment/service options, and related issues.
Working knowledge of SCS programs and services, policy, and procedure.
Working knowledge of applicable regulations and licensure standards.
Good interpersonal skills and written and oral communication skills.

Position requires lifting of 20 pounds maximum, with frequent lifting and/or carrying of items weighing up to 10 pounds, or requires significant periods of walking or standing.
Normal tasks may involve exposure to blood, bodily fluids, or tissue.
May involve 24-hour on-call responsibilities.
Reliable transportation for frequent travel.

jobs.title: Case Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

What You'll Do

T he Case Manager is responsible for developing and monitoring comprehensive participant service plans in collaboration with assigned participants. This includes, but is not necessarily limited to, internal and external referrals for services to stabilize medical and mental health conditions, barrier removal, job readiness coaching, job placement assistance, and retention services.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Initiate services for participants following their clinical assessment or clinical reassessment, providing orientation to services, explaining their rights and responsibilities, and answering questions.
Develop and monitor wellness plans on behalf of participants with untreated or unstable medical and/or mental health conditions adversely impacting employability. This includes coordinating referrals to community-based medical and mental health providers.
Regularly meet with assigned participants to monitor progress and compliance with wellness plans, as well as to assist with mitigating barriers to employment. These incudes, but is certainly not limited to housing, domestic violence, childcare, transportation, and reasonable accommodations.
Conduct regular phone follow-up appointments with participants to assess progress toward wellness plan goals.
Outreach to participants who have failed to comply with mandatory appointments and other program requirements to successfully re-engage them with their wellness services.
Communicate with external medical and mental health providers to ensure participant compliance and timely completion of wellness plans.
Provide intensive individual coaching for participants in job search activities and assist participants with issues pertaining to work-related and transitional benefits.
Case conference with other WeCARE service providers on an as needed basis, including vocational evaluators, work readiness and computer instructors, job placement coordinators, job preparation counselors and WEP specialists.
Document participant services and activities in Fedcap and HRA management information systems, including, but not limited to SEAMS and FedcapCARES .

You're a great fit for this role if you have:

Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field, such as psychology, vocational rehabilitation, or occupational rehabilitation. MSW or master’s degree in a related field preferred.
One (1) year of case management or related experience.
Bilingual (English Spanish) preferred.

Compensation

$23.08-$24.04/hr.

Equal Opportunity Employer

About Us

Mission:
To help people who face barriers to work obtain employment and achieve self-sufficiency through innovative job training, placement and support services.

Community Work Services (CWS) was founded in 1877 as the Cooperative Society of Visitors Among the Poor of Boston to provide services to the poor of Boston and address the roots of poverty through employment, education, and housing improvements. Its founder, Annie Fields, is said to have been a transitional figure in the development of a professional social-service network. Mrs. Fields hoped to apply business principles and efficiency to benevolent activities and charity work. Today CWS provides job placement, training and support services in the Boston area.

Community Work Services joined The Fedcap Group in 2013.

Website: www.cwsnewengland.org

The Jail to Work Case Manager in Blount County serves as a case manager that provides case coordination using a social model approach to a predetermined number of adult women.
The case manager provides information and referral, agency linkage, advocacy, and follow-up services as defined by the Program Case Manager Service Plan for female inmates at the Blount County Jail.
The case manager must embrace the key values of recovery and case management: empowerment, normalization, rehabilitation, and continuity of care.
The holder of this position will be required to do the following and other responsibilities as assigned by his/her direct supervisor.
Must maintain appropriate chart records and document case management and group meeting notes per agency standards.
Must complete all documentation in a timely manner and according to agency standards.
Must participate in direct supervision with program supervisor and director, as necessary.
Must interface with community agencies and referral sources to coordinate care.
Must provide Medication monitoring, therapeutic support and crisis intervention as needed.
Must participate in weekly treatment team meetings with relevant staff for coordination of care.
Must uphold professional ethical standards and centers policy and procedures as well as CARF standards.

The Community Engagement Coordinator will strengthen the relationships and visibility of the school through active service and engagement in the community that meets or exceeds practice expectations (i.e. community engagement accreditation requirements). jobs.title: CKP Ryan White Medical Case Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

JOB SUMMARY

The Medical Case Manager (MCM) is responsible for providing comprehensive, client-centered Medical Case Management services to individuals living with HIV/AIDS enrolled in the Ryan White Part B Region 3 Program. The Medical Case Manager supports clients in achieving optimal health outcomes through assessment, care planning, treatment adherence support, linkage to medical and behavioral health services, and ongoing coordination of care.

The Medical Case Manager works collaboratively with interdisciplinary care teams, community providers, and support service agencies to ensure continuity of care and improve viral suppression and retention in care outcomes for clients. Services are delivered in accordance with Ryan White Part B Standards of Care, HRSA/HAB National Monitoring Standards, HIPAA regulations, and Community Health Center policies and procedures.

Role And Responsibilities

Medical Case Management Services
Conduct comprehensive client assessments within required timelines to identify medical, psychosocial, behavioral health, housing, financial, transportation, substance use, and other service needs.
Utilize the Ryan White Medical Case Management Triage Model to determine appropriate levels of case management services.
Develop individualized care plans in collaboration with clients and interdisciplinary providers.
Maintain ongoing monthly contact with clients to monitor progress toward care plan goals and address barriers to care.
Provide treatment adherence counseling and education regarding HIV disease management, medications, viral suppression, prevention strategies, and overall wellness.
Coordinate timely access to medical care, behavioral health services, specialty care, substance use treatment, housing services, transportation, insurance assistance, and other support services.
Facilitate referrals and follow-up with internal and external providers to ensure continuity of care.
Monitor client engagement in HIV medical care and support retention in care efforts.
Conduct reassessments and update care plans at minimum every six (6) months or as clinically indicated.
Participate in discharge planning and transitions of care in collaboration with supervisors and care teams.
Advocate on behalf of clients to reduce barriers and improve access to medically appropriate services.

Documentation and Data Management
Maintain accurate, timely, and complete documentation in electronic health records and required Ryan White data systems.
Enter all service encounters, care plans, referrals, and case notes within five (5) business days of service delivery.
Document face-to-face encounters, telehealth visits, phone contacts, referrals, care coordination activities, and treatment adherence services.
Collect and maintain required Ryan White Part B program data, including:
Client demographics
Units of service
Viral load outcomes
Hepatitis B and C screening status
Tuberculosis testing
Mental health and substance use screenings
HIV risk reduction counseling

Participate in Ryan White Services Report (RSR) reporting and other required program reporting activities.
Ensure confidentiality and compliance with HIPAA, Connecticut HIV confidentiality laws, and organizational policies.

Care Coordination and Community Collaboration
Collaborate with medical providers, nurses, behavioral health clinicians, pharmacists, outreach workers, and community agencies to coordinate comprehensive care.
Maintain active referral relationships with hospitals, public health departments, shelters, behavioral health providers, correctional facilities, HIV testing sites, and community organizations.
Participate in interdisciplinary case conferences, quality improvement activities, and care coordination meetings.
Support clients with benefits counseling and linkage to Medicaid, Medicare, insurance programs, pharmaceutical assistance programs, and other entitlement services.

Quality Management and Compliance
Participate in Clinical Quality Management (CQM) and Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) initiatives.
Assist with program monitoring activities, audits, corrective action plans, and quality improvement projects.
Attend required Ryan White Part B Region 3 trainings, provider meetings, and professional development opportunities.
Participate in statewide planning and community engagement activities, including the CT HIV Planning Consortium when assigned.
Maintain compliance with all Ryan White payer-of-last-resort requirements and program eligibility standards.

Caseload Expectations
Maintain a minimum active caseload of:
50 clients for Traditional Medical Case Management services
Complete approximately 1,500 client encounters annually.
Perform special assignments, projects, and other duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Nursing, Human Services, Public Health, Psychology, or related health/human services field from an accredited college or university required.
Minimum of one (1) year of experience providing case management, care coordination, or client services in healthcare, HIV services, behavioral health, or community-based settings preferred.
Experience working with individuals living with HIV/AIDS, underserved populations, LGBTQ+ communities, individuals with substance use disorders, mental health conditions, housing instability, or chronic medical conditions preferred.
Bilingual English/Spanish preferred.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Knowledge of HIV/AIDS treatment, prevention, and Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program services preferred.
Strong understanding of trauma-informed care, motivational interviewing, harm reduction, and client-centered practices.
Knowledge of community resources, entitlement programs, and healthcare systems.
Excellent organizational, communication, documentation, and time-management skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and maintain accurate records in electronic systems.

PURPOSE STATEMENT:

The Case Manager supports the department by providing case management to the different units within the facility. As a member of the treatment team, is responsible for coordinating care across multiple providers to ensure clients receive support identified within the individualize treatment plan. Responsible for the overall discharge and aftercare planning needs and placement of the client. Maintains ongoing communication with the treatment team. Maintains routine contact with referral sources and providers while maintaining resource file. Participates in quality care monitoring for the department.

Roles and Responsibilities:

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Develops and implements appropriate activities and/or programs within their scope of practice. Implements services to clients in accordance with their individualized service plan (ISP).
Collaborates with the client and client’s family or significant others to implement an effective service plan, explaining the available options to the team, including the advantages and disadvantages of each option.
Maintains the client’s comprehensive clinical record, including documentation of activities performed as part of the service delivery process (e.g., assessments, provision of services, coordination of care, discharge planning) and client’s progress toward their recovery.
Works collaboratively with the clinical team to engage, educate, communicate, and coordinate care with client, their family, behavioral and general medical health care providers, community resources and others to ensure that all services prescribed in the individualized service plan (ISP) are implemented.
Assures that discharge planning begins at admission. Obtains collateral input from providers and supports.
Ensures all appropriate referrals for identified services on the service plan are made and coordinated with service providers via contracted network providers or community resources; Ensures all covered services identified on the service plan are evaluated and updated monthly.
Coordinates referral or completes the screening and assessment on all clients on caseload for financial entitlements (AHCCCS, SSI/SSD etc.); completes AHCCCS applications on all clients on caseload meeting criteria.
Ensures the development and implementation of transition, discharge, and aftercare plans prior to discontinuation of behavioral health services.
Ensures all contact with referral source and/or other treatment providers is done within designated time frame and documented accordingly.
Employs appropriate crisis intervention techniques as needed.
Communicates appropriate client information to the treatment team; participates in team discussion and evaluation of client goals, objectives and motivations.

This position is an Individual Contributor.

jobs.title: Med-Legal Case Manager
jobs.description:
Ignite Practice Growth

Employment Type: Full-Time (Monday - Friday 8-5)

Department: Med-Legal / Personal Injury Operations

Compensation: Based on experience

Benefits: PTO, Health, Dental, Vision, Short-term Disability, 401(k) + matching

About Ignite Practice Growth

Ignite Practice Growth helps medical practices improve operational performance, patient coordination, and growth. We work with healthcare organizations that serve patients involved in personal injury and medical-legal cases, helping create efficient systems that support providers, patients, attorneys, and other stakeholders throughout the continuum of care.

We are seeking a highly organized, proactive Med-Legal Case Manager to coordinate personal injury and medical-legal cases from intake through treatment completion and case resolution.

This role is ideal for someone with experience in personal injury case management, medical case management, legal case coordination, healthcare administration, or medical-legal operations who understands how to keep complex cases moving while maintaining accurate documentation and professional communication.

Position Summary

The Med-Legal Case Manager serves as a central point of coordination for active personal injury and medical-legal cases.

You will work across medical practices, patients, attorneys and law firms, providers, and internal operations teams to help ensure cases progress efficiently, documentation is accurate, communication is timely, and outstanding issues are identified before they become problems.

This is a case ownership position, not simply an administrative support role. The successful candidate will be comfortable managing a case portfolio, following up consistently, identifying stalled cases, maintaining detailed records, and communicating professionally with both healthcare and legal professionals.

Key Responsibilities

Personal Injury & MedLegal Case Management
Manage assigned personal injury and medicallegal cases throughout the patient treatment lifecycle.
Monitor case status, treatment progression, referrals, appointments, and outstanding case requirements.
Maintain accurate and current case notes, documentation, contact information, and status updates.
Identify cases that have stalled or require additional followup and proactively work toward resolution.
Maintain organized case workflows and followup schedules to prevent missed deadlines or communication gaps.
Attorney & Law Firm Coordination
Communicate professionally with attorneys, paralegals, legal assistants, and law firm case managers regarding patient and case status.
Coordinate appropriate requests for case information and documentation.
Maintain accurate attorney and law firm information within applicable systems.
Develop strong working relationships with legal partners while maintaining appropriate professional and compliance boundaries.
Escalate complex case issues when necessary.
Patient & Treatment Coordination
Support communication necessary to keep patients progressing through prescribed treatment plans.
Coordinate with clinic teams and providers regarding patient status, referrals, treatment progression, and outstanding needs.
Help identify missed appointments, treatment gaps, or other issues that may interfere with continuity of care.
Facilitate communication among appropriate parties while respecting patient privacy and HIPAA requirements.
Medical Documentation & Case Support
Help coordinate requests involving medical records, bills, treatment documentation, referrals, and other caserelated information.
Monitor outstanding documentation and follow up with responsible parties.
Maintain organized case records to support efficient response to authorized requests.
Assist with case status reporting and internal documentation requirements.
Case Tracking & Reporting
Maintain accurate case information in CRM, case management, and/or practice management systems.
Track assigned caseload and key case milestones.
Monitor outstanding tasks and followup dates.
Provide management with updates regarding case volume, aging cases, treatment gaps, unresolved issues, and other relevant trends.
Participate in efforts to improve case management processes, workflows, and communication standards.

What We're Looking For

The ideal candidate combines strong organization with persistence and professional communication. You should be someone who takes ownership of your cases rather than waiting to be told what requires attention.

Preferred Experience

Experience in personal injury, medicallegal case management, legal case management, healthcare administration, medical practice operations, or a related field.
Experience communicating with personal injury attorneys, law firms, paralegals, medical providers, or healthcare practices.
Familiarity with the lifecycle of a personal injury patient or case.
Experience managing multiple active cases, accounts, patients, or client relationships simultaneously.
Experience with CRM, case management, EHR/EMR, or practice management software.
Understanding of HIPAA and confidential medical information.

Core Competencies
Successful candidates will demonstrate:

Exceptional organization and attention to detail.
Strong written and verbal communication.
Professional phone and email communication skills.
Ability to manage a highvolume caseload and competing priorities.
Consistent followthrough and accountability.
Ability to identify problems and take appropriate action without constant supervision.
Strong documentation and recordkeeping habits.
Ability to communicate effectively with attorneys, healthcare providers, patients, and internal teams.
Comfort working in a fastpaced, growthoriented organization.
Sound judgment when handling confidential medical and legal information.

Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent required; associate or bachelor's degree preferred.
Prior experience in personal injury, healthcare, legal services, medical case management, or case coordination strongly preferred.
Strong computer skills and ability to learn multiple technology platforms.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and/or Google Workspace.
Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and comply with applicable HIPAA and privacy requirements.

What Success Looks Like
A successful Med-Legal Case Manager at Ignite Practice Growth:

Knows the current status of their assigned cases.
Follows up before issues become urgent.
Keeps case documentation accurate and current.
Communicates effectively with law firms and medical teams.
Identifies treatment or communication gaps quickly.
Maintains consistent case progression.
Takes ownership of problems through resolution.
Provides management with reliable visibility into the case portfolio.

Why Join Ignite Practice Growth?

This position provides an opportunity to become an important part of a growing organization operating at the intersection of healthcare, personal injury, and medical-legal case management.

You will have the opportunity to build expertise in medical-legal operations, develop relationships across healthcare and legal organizations, and grow professionally as Ignite Practice Growth continues to expand.

We value people who are organized, accountable, solutions-oriented, and committed to delivering a high level of service.

The Care Manager provides comprehensive case management and care coordination services for elderly individuals and adults with physical and intellectual disabilities, helping them live as independently as possible in the community. This role combines social work case management, member assessments, and collaborative care planning within a mission-driven, team-oriented environment. The position is full-time, primarily weekday-based, and supports a partnership program serving members in Milwaukee and the surrounding area.

Responsibilities

Manage an assigned caseload of program members in collaboration with an RN Care Manager, ensuring timely and effective delivery of services.
Complete comprehensive member assessments, including physical, social, and psychosocial evaluations, to determine needs and appropriate services.
Develop and maintain member-centered care plans that promote independence and support individual goals and preferences.
Perform and document functional screens as required, including certified functional screener responsibilities when applicable.

Job Summary

Primary point of contact for both new hire orientation and student programming within the health system. This position leads New Employee Orientation, ensuring a welcoming and comprehensive onboarding experience for all incoming staff. The Coordinator also oversees all aspects of the student program—including onboarding and orienting students, creating and managing clinical rotation slots across nursing floors and other disciplines, and serving as the primary liaison between academic partners and the health system. This role networks with clinical leadership to understand workforce and educational needs, manages affiliation agreements and school contracts in collaboration with the legal department and risk management, and facilitates shadow and clinical rotation requests by connecting requestors with appropriate discipline leadership.

New Hire Orientation Leadership-

Plans, designs, and continuously improves New Employee Orientation content, incorporating adult learning principles and a variety of instructional modalities.
Distributes a weekly orientation logistics and roster email to all relevant stakeholders prior to each orientation session.
Assigns and monitors required learning modules in HealthStream (LMS) for all new hires, ensuring timely completion in accordance with policy and regulatory requirements.
Oversees scheduling, room reservations, guest speakers, and materials management for all orientation sessions.
Evaluates orientation effectiveness through feedback mechanisms and adjusts programming to reflect current organizational policies, regulatory requirements, and best practices.

Student Program Oversight-

Onboards and orients incoming students, ensuring all organizational screening, compliance, and credentialing requirements are met prior to the start of each rotation.
Develops and maintains current student orientation materials, policies, and guidelines.
Creates, manages, and monitors clinical rotation slots on nursing floors and other clinical units.
Communicates regularly with school program directors and clinical leadership to align student placement with unit capacity and organizational needs.
Serves as the organizational liaison between the institution and the academic partner when concerns arise.

Academic Partner & Liaison-

Networks with clinical leadership across disciplines to understand current workforce needs and capacity for student and shadow experiences, adjusting the student program accordingly.
Facilitates shadow requests by connecting requestors to appropriate discipline leadership to assess feasibility of shadow or clinical rotation opportunities.
Partners with Human Resources and clinical leadership to leverage the student pipeline as a recruitment strategy, encouraging students to consider the health system as a future employer.
Serves on advisory boards or participates in school-based committees to maintain academic relationships and help align curriculum with evidence-based practice and organizational needs.
Partners with the Nurse Residency Coordinator and other Talent Management stakeholders to strengthen the continuum from student to new hire.

Contracts & Affiliation Agreement Management-

Initiates, reviews, and updates affiliation agreements and clinical education contracts in collaboration with risk management, the legal department, and organizational leadership.
Serves as the primary organizational liaison to the legal department for all school and academic partner contracts, tracking status and ensuring timely renewals.
Maintains a centralized, organized record system for all active and archived affiliation agreements.
Communicates contract requirements and updates to relevant internal and external stakeholders in a timely manner.

Professional Development-

Maintains current knowledge of trends in talent management, new hire onboarding, academic partnerships, and healthcare education.
Demonstrates ability to utilize available resources to establish and maintain best practices for student programming and new hire orientation.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage priorities independently
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint)
Experience with HealthStream LMS required, or demonstrated ability to learn within 90 days
Demonstrated ability to build collaborative relationships with internal clinical leadership and external academic partners
Knowledge of adult learning principles and ability to apply them in orientation and educational program design
Ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and handle sensitive information with professionalism

Bachelor's degree in Education, Healthcare Administration, Nursing, or related field required
Master's degree preferred

Experience

Minimum of 2 years experience in healthcare education, talent management, student program coordination, or a closely related field required
Experience coordinating orientation programs or managing academic partnerships preferred

As an LMSW/LMGW Inpatient Case Manager, you will serve as a member of the Case Management Team. Facilitates the delivery of quality, cost effective, patient-centered care from pre-admission through post-discharge. Ensures the care is designed to meet individualized patient outcomes. Monitors the care and services delivered to selected patient populations during the acute hospital stay, promotes effective case management and utilization of resources, and works to achieve optimal clinical and resource outcomes.

Join one of the largest healthcare systems in the Baltimore-Washington metro region, also recognized as one of the "Healthiest Maryland Businesses". Apply today and learn how MedStar Health can be your next great career move!

Primary Duties

Collaborates with the multidisciplinary health care team to develop and coordinate the plan of care. Demonstrates the ability to develop a plan of care that addresses needs across the continuum; develop long- and short-term goals with specific time frames for resolution; identify specific services to be provided in the care plan; include the family/care-giver in the plan of care; and show life planning contingencies such as power of attorney and/or advance directives. Collaborates with and completes referrals to appropriate community agencies for assistance based on patient needs. Initiates referrals in a timely manner. Uses responses to help patients resume life in the community and/or adjust to lifestyle changes.
Communicates daily with direct caregivers and case management triad regarding patient and family responses to plan of care, identification of problems, discharge planning, and payor concerns such as LOS. Identifies delays in care and quality/risk issues and communicates information to appropriate individuals and departments. Completes psychosocial history or socioeconomic assessment as determined by healthcare team or high-risk indicators. Adheres to all policies and procedures regarding documentation and confidentiality of information. Demonstrates knowledge of the dynamics of abuse/neglect, including identification and reporting laws. Coordinates investigating law enforcement, protection agencies, hospital security, risk management, and healthcare teams. Effectively intervenes with patient/family in resolving emotional/behavioral obstacles to patient's progress, recovery, and disposition. Initiates and participates in multidisciplinary discharge planning rounds and collaborates with internal and external health care providers, patients, and families to develop comprehensive discharge plans.

Experience in social work in a hospital setting preferred.
Experience in care/case management preferred.

Manage the major events calendar.
Identify opportunities to standardize policies and automate processes.
Provide guidance to the Administrative Core Team for completing tasks including event planning, office management, and financial disbursements.

Bachelor's degree and 3+ years of related experience or an equivalent combination of education and related experience required.

Experience maintaining relationships and channels of communication at multiple levels and with diverse groups inside and outside the organization.
Experience executing logistics related to academic programming and events.
Experience delivering presentations to audiences at multiple levels.

jobs.title: Program Manager - Scholarly Engagement and Post-Baccalaureate Success
jobs.description:
Summary

Job Summary

The Student Academic Success Center (SASC) at CU Boulder invites applications for The Program Manager – Scholarly Engagement and Post-Baccalaureate Success position! This is a part-time university staff position in the Student Academic Success Center (SASC) that supports a research-intensive learning program and assigned scholarly engagement initiatives. Reporting to the Program Director, this position serves on a three-member team that provides day-to-day oversight and operational support for the portfolio’s programs and services.

The Program Manager serves as the primary day-to-day coordinator for the Puksta Scholars Program, with direction from the Program Director, supports scholarly engagement and post-baccalaureate success initiatives across SASC. Responsibilities include recruitment and onboarding; advising and coaching; workshops, activities, and events; communications, records management, and assessment support; and coordination of student participation in high-impact scholarly engagement and post-baccalaureate preparation experiences.

This position helps implement upper-division programming in scholarly activity and civic learning; faculty mentorship and undergraduate research; fellowship applications and graduate or professional school preparation; and other enrichment experiences. The position coordinates assigned program processes; maintains effective working relationships with educational opportunity programs, campus offices, research faculty, and community partners; and recommends improvements based on student needs, success outcomes, and operational efficiencies. This position requires collegiality and professionalism; sound judgment and strong organization; initiative and problem-solving skills.

CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

Who We Are

The Student Academic Success Center (SASC) is an educational opportunity center in the Office of Undergraduate Education within Academic Affairs at the University of Colorado Boulder. For more than 60 years, SASC has supported student success through a mission-inspired learning community of students, faculty, and staff whose backgrounds and pathways are historically non-traditional in higher education.

Within SASC, the Scholarly Engagement and Post-Baccalaureate portfolio comprises the McNair Scholars Program which serves 25 students engaged in undergraduate research, and the Puksta Scholars Program which serves 16 students engaged in community-based projects. Together, these two research-focused programs and expanded upper-division services contribute to the pre-college to post-baccalaureate pathway in SASC by advancing scholarly engagement, civic learning, and preparation for post-baccalaureate opportunities for our students.

Responsibilities

What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be

Program and Portfolio Operations

Facilitates day-to-day operations for the Puksta Scholars Program and assigned portfolio initiatives across the academic year service cycle.
Responsible for recruitment and outreach; application and selection; onboarding and orientation; and year-round engagement and retention of Puksta Scholars.
Leads the Puksta Scholars Program plan of operations in collaboration with the Program Director, including advising support, enrichments, and student success initiatives.
Coordinates program calendars, events, retreats, meetings, and workshops that support scholarly engagement, civic learning, academic achievement, and post-baccalaureate preparation.
Serves as the primary operational contact for Puksta Scholars and coordinates routine communication, follow-up, referrals, and resolution of program questions.
Supports new upper-division scholarly engagement initiatives by supporting logistics, materials, events, and other assigned components.

Student Engagement and Enrichment

Provides high-contact student support that strengthens students’ academic, scholarly, civic, and post-baccalaureate development.
Provides individualized advising, coaching, and developmental support to Puksta Scholars and students participating in assigned scholarly engagement initiatives.
Helps students develop and monitor academic, scholarly, civic, leadership, research, and post-baccalaureate goals.
Connects students with faculty mentors and research opportunities; scholarships and fellowships; graduate or professional preparation resources; career development, academic support, and other campus resources.
Facilitates educational experiences and community-building activities that strengthen scholarly engagement, civic learning, belonging, leadership development, and post-baccalaureate preparation.
Monitors student engagement, identifies barriers to persistence or participation, and coordinates with the Program Director appropriate interventions and referrals.

Assessment and Improvement

Manages records, data collection, documentation, and reporting processes that support assessment, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Maintains accurate student records, participation data, advising documentation, program files, calendars, handbooks, forms, resource materials, curricular or co-curricular materials, and assessment data in accordance with university or sponsor policies and program requirements.
Facilitates collection of participation, engagement, satisfaction, academic progress, and outcome data for program and assigned scholarly engagement initiatives.
Supports the Program Director with the assessment cycle, including data collection, organization, and preliminary analysis to inform program review and improvement.
Identifies operational trends and student needs and shares recommendations with The Program Director to improve program processes, services, and student experiences.
Supports preparation of internal reports, program summaries, assessment materials, sponsor updates, and other documentation required for planning and evaluation.

Communications and Partnerships

Coordinates communications, outreach, and working relationships that promote participation and expand student access to scholarly and post-baccalaureate opportunities.
Develops routine communications with Puksta Scholars and other participants in assigned scholarly engagement initiatives through appropriate digital, print, presentation, and outreach channels.
Coordinates recruitment and outreach communications, including clear, accessible, and student-centered materials for programs, events, research opportunities, fellowships, and graduate preparation activities.
Maintains assigned communication resources, including web content, calendars, newsletters, resource guides, and related materials.
Assists the Program Director with maintaining working relationships with department-based faculty, research and graduate education partners, scholarship and fellowship programs, career services, libraries, and other campus and community partners to support student referrals, programming, and access to opportunities.
Works with campus partners, in consultation with the Program Director, to connect students with research projects, scholarly events, post-baccalaureate preparation, and related opportunities; supports program and assigned portfolio initiatives at relevant campus events, meetings, orientations, and professional development activities.

Resource and Team Support

Provides administrative, fiscal, and team support for effective, compliant, and student-centered program delivery.
Coordinates routine administrative and fiscal processes related to events, purchasing, travel, stipends, scholarships, and program activities.
Tracks expenditures, student-support resources, and program deliverables to support budget monitoring, reconciliation, and planning.
Supports scheduling, onboarding, and communication with graduate assistants, student employees, peer mentors, volunteers, faculty mentors, instructors, and other personnel or volunteers as assigned.
Provides logistical support for team meetings, trainings, retreats, professional development activities, and program planning.
Maintains confidentiality and follows university, sponsor, and program requirements when handling student, financial, program, and institutional information.

What You Should Know

This part-time role will work 20 hours per week and follow a hybrid work schedule with 3 days on-site and 2 days remote.

What We Can Offer

The annual salary for this position is $28,600.

Benefits

At the University of Colorado Boulder , we are committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical, dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class outdoor recreation. In fact, CU Boulder has been named one of Forbes' America's Best Large Employers , ranking #4 among large employers in Colorado and #28 among universities nationwide. Explore additional perks and programs through the CU Advantage program.

Be Statements

Be creative. Be impactful. Be Boulder.

What We Require

A bachelor's degree or equivalent in any field.
A minimum of two (2) years of student-centered experience such as advising, tutoring, or work study supervision at a 2-year or 4- year higher education institution. A minimum of one (1) year of administrative experience with duties in budgeting, record keeping, and event planning.

What You Will Need

Knowledge of TRiO legislation and regulations; or knowledge of Colorado Department of Education (CDE) and Colorado Commission on Higher Education (CCHE) policies and standards; or immediate capacity to learn.
Practical experience working with TRiO-eligible students and/or life experience as a TRiO- eligible student. Skills in data management and social media marketing.
Professional knowledge of standard processes in post-baccalaureate or "alt-ac" preparation for special populations.
Experience in facilitating multi-modality workshops and services for on-campus and on-line participants.
Abilities in creating and sustaining networks, affiliations, and partnerships with campus units, student groups, and community partners

What We Would Like You To Have

A master’s degree in any field. TRiO or other educational opportunity program alumni status or one or more years of higher education teaching experience may be substituted for up to 1 year of the 2-year minimum years of experience

Special Instructions

To Apply, Please Submit The Following Materials

A current resume.
A cover letter that specifically tells us how your background and experience align with the requirements, qualifications, and responsibilities of the position.

We may request references at a later time.

Please apply by October 21, 2026
for consideration.

Note: Application materials will not be accepted via email. For consideration, please apply through CU Boulder Jobs.

In compliance with the Colorado Job Application Fairness Act, in any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.

Job Summary

The Psychosocial Research Program at Butler Hospital is looking to hire one full-time research assistant to work on a project related to implementing a suicide intervention in a psychiatric emergency department setting. There may also be opportunities available to work on additional projects in our lab focused on implementation of a tablet-based suicide prevention in a crisis stabilization setting, and identification of novel risk factors for suicide using laboratory-based behavioral and physiological assessments, smartphone technology, and smartwatches. The Principal Investigators in our research lab are Michael Armey, Ph.D., Chris Hughes, Ph.D., Heather Schatten, Ph.D., and Gemma Wallace, Ph.D.

Butler Hospital is the major affiliated teaching hospital for psychiatry and behavioral health of The Warren Alpert Medical School of Brown University, located in Providence, RI. Butler Hospital is one of the earliest psychiatric facilities established in the United States. The Psychosocial Research Program at Butler is one of several active research groups at the hospital. Dr. Ivan Miller is the director, and the program is comprised of academic psychologists, postdoctoral fellows, research assistants, master’s-level interventionists, and project coordinators. Research in this group is currently funded by numerous federal and foundation grants, and most of this work centers on suicide prevention, post-hospital transitions, technology-assisted assessment and intervention, mood and psychotic disorders, and comorbid conditions conducted in a variety of clinical settings.
